clue.text: Unswerving vision about ret-regrade art

indicators.note: the word for vision goes about, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word art is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone with a steady eye passes judgment on backward-looking artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrograde' turns ART into TRA, which 'about' places inside SIGHT after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A line that never swerves is direct, without bends.

clue.text: A Communist about to take it easy, but seized by the authorities

indicators.note: the word for Communist goes about, around, the phrase for relaxing

parts.note: a Red is a Communist
to rest is to take it easy

explanation.surface: A party member planning to relax finds the police have other ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts REST inside RED, giving R-REST-ED after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone detained by the police has been taken into custody.

clue.text: Wooden salver designed for the smoke-room, maybe

definitions.text: Wooden salver designed for the smoke-room, maybe

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber, so wooden suggests ash
a salver is a flat serving tray

explanation.surface: A carved wooden plate is made for use in the smoking room.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle for cigarette stubs is a dish suited to a smoking lounge, and here could be a wooden platter.

clue.text: Quick-firing weapon inwardly all right, though in need of repair, apparently

indicators.note: inwardly says the second piece sits inside the weapon's name

parts.note: the Bren is a light machine gun
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A machine gun seems fine inside but actually needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bren gun was a British light machine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged and not working needs mending.

clue.text: At last ordered out of federal country?

indicators.note: ordered out means set out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has finally been expelled from a federal nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to a state, as within a federation of states.

clue.text: Unusually stern treaties that add to the burdens of debtor countries?

definitions.text: that add to the burdens of debtor countries

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: Harsh international agreements weigh heavily on nations that owe money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges STERN TREATIES, thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges on borrowed money increase what indebted nations must repay.

clue.text: The quality most needed for becoming an investigative journalist, presumably

definitions.text: The quality most needed for becoming an investigative journalist, presumably

parts.words: The quality most needed for becoming an investigative journalist, presumably
parts.note: a reporter who digs into stories needs a curious, questioning temperament

explanation.definitionFit: A curious intellect that keeps asking questions suits a reporter digging for stories.

clue.text: What idle hands should be given, yet it's no good to them, in a way

definitions.text: What idle hands should be given

indicators.note: in a way here means arranged another way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Idle hands need occupying, though the job offered is no use to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges IT'S NO GOOD with THEM; the 'to' between them is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle people need an occupation or task to keep them busy.

clue.text: Type of infantry battle formation now considered old-fashioned

definitions.meaning: a hollow block of foot soldiers facing outwards, used against cavalry
a slang sense: a conventional, out-of-date person or thing

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a four-sided defensive troop formation and someone dull and conventional.

clue.text: To convey it back to me will evidently be a slow job

parts.note: to take something is to convey it

indicators.note: back says the word it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Carrying something back to the speaker will clearly be a lengthy task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IT into TI, placed between TAKE and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A job that is not quick requires patience and hours.

clue.text: The schoolmaster's nominal entitlement

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher by a title, which is also the title of a knight

explanation.definitionFit: Schoolchildren address a male teacher this way, and it is also a knight's honorific.

clue.text: Abnormally gifted children may if the lesson is boring

definitions.text: children may if the lesson is boring

indicators.note: abnormally signals the letters in an abnormal order

explanation.surface: Unusually talented pupils grow restless when the class is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Bored children squirm and move restlessly in their seats.

clue.text: Ring-marked nun involved in a garbled tale

indicators.note: in places the involved piece inside the garbled one
a garbled account has its parts confused, so these letters are mixed
involved means tangled, so these letters are shuffled too

explanation.surface: A ringed nun gets caught up in a confused story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns NUN into NNU; 'garbled' turns A TALE into ALATE; 'in' places NNU after its first A.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoological term for having bands or circles of colour, as on some worms.

clue.text: Swiss tourist centre

parts.note: a canton of central Switzerland by Lake Lucerne, popular with visitors

explanation.definitionFit: A central Swiss canton on Lake Lucerne, linked with William Tell, draws visitors.

clue.text: A guinea-fowl party held by the Milk Marketing Board?

indicators.note: held by says the party is one put on by the following body

parts.note: the Milk Marketing Board's slogan was 'drinka pinta milka day', so its product is a pinta
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A guinea-fowl at a function hosted by a dairy authority.
explanation.walkthrough: A PINTA is a British word for a pint of milk; the Milk Marketing Board was the UK body that sold milk.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Portuguese-derived name for the speckled guinea-fowl.

clue.text: I'm after a purpose in Life, possibly …

indicators.note: after says the first word given comes after the second one in the answer

parts.note: I'm gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone is seeking a meaning to their existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal or ambition is what one strives for in life.

clue.text: In intellect it led the world a few generations ago!

definitions.text: In intellect it led the world a few generations ago!

indicators.note: in places the little word inside the word for intellect

parts.note: brain means intellect

explanation.surface: A nostalgic boast that the nation once led the world in brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Kingdom's homeland was a leading world power in the Victorian era.

clue.text: … that would make a fitting subject for a documentary

definitions.text: … that would make a fitting subject for a documentary

parts.words: … that would make a fitting subject for a documentary
parts.note: factual films show actual events and people rather than fiction

explanation.definitionFit: Documentaries depict actual existence rather than invented drama.

clue.text: Government-run cash nishing store

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Government-run cash nishing store': 'nishing' is garbled, a word cut short (perhaps 'furnishing'), and no scan is held to restore it.

clue.text: I'm plied with candy and simply full of energy!

indicators.note: plied suggests the letters are worked over and bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: A child stuffed with sweets becomes hyperactive.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful, lively person bursts with vigour.

clue.text: Anguish about a border plant with yellow flowers

indicators.note: the word for anguish goes about, around, the word for border

parts.note: agony is anguish
a rim is a border

explanation.surface: A gardener frets about a yellow-flowered border plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RIM inside AGONY after AG. 'Border' looks like the garden bed, but it gives RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayside herb of the rose family bearing spikes of small golden blooms.

clue.text: Slid uneasily round an off, shore possession

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the little word
uneasily suggests the letters shifting uncomfortably out of place

explanation.surface: A nervous slip goes round a country's overseas holding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasily' turns SLID into ISLD, and 'round' puts AN between L and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory surrounded by sea is a land mass held offshore.

clue.text: Start out with fixed determination?

parts.note: taken as written
to be set on something is to have a fixed resolve

explanation.surface: Someone sets off resolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: SET OUT also means start out, which gives the clue its surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of an undertaking is its opening.

clue.text: Seek and get satisfaction from Geneva

indicators.note: from here means made from the letters of the city, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pursues redress in a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a loose anagram signal: the letters of GENEVA are worked into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact retribution is to obtain redress for a wrong.

clue.text: Nothing left in

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Nothing left in': NI + L needs 'in' reversed with no reversal indicator, so 'left' would do two jobs (L and the signal).

clue.text: Verdi heroine tragically destined to live at variance

indicators.note: at variance means in disagreement, signalling letters set apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: An operatic heroine is doomed to a life of conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The doomed courtesan in La Traviata, who dies of consumption.

clue.text: Tissue of lies on a medical injury

indicators.note: a tissue is a woven fabric, so the words are woven into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor's report on a wound is a pack of falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tissue of' rearranges LIES ON; 'tissue' looks medical, but it is the weaving signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors call an area of damaged body tissue a wound or abnormality by this term.

clue.text: Classical account of a poet who went through hell to achieve fame

definitions.text: Classical account of a poet who went through hell to achieve fame

parts.words: Classical account of a poet who went through hell to achieve fame
parts.note: the Italian poet's epic describes his own journey through the underworld, the work that made him famous

explanation.definitionFit: The first part of the Divine Comedy recounts the Florentine poet's descent through the underworld.
